What we offer for our full-time, regular employees

• 🏢 Our in-office work policy is designed to keep you connected - with four days a week in the office and Fridays from home for those near one of our offices, plus team and company-wide events depending on location.

• 💻 Benefits that support your work and life, including backup child, elder, and pet care and subsidized commuter benefits for eligible employees.

• ✨ Comprehensive health, financial, and wellbeing benefits designed to support you at every stage of life.

• 🏝 Generous vacation policy and company-wide paid days off

• 🫂 1% of your time off to support local community organizations of your choice

• 👟 Annual wellness stipend to use towards eligible wellness related expenses

• 👶 Up to 22 weeks of paid parental leave for birthing parents and 12 weeks of paid parental leave for non-birthing parents

• 👪 Access to family planning reimbursement

• 💚 A challenging and fulfilling opportunity to join one of the most experienced teams in FinTech and help millions unlock financial progress

We know that great work can’t be done without a diverse team and inclusive environment. That’s why we specifically look for individuals of varying strengths, skills, backgrounds, and ideas to join our team. We believe this gives us a competitive advantage to better serve our members and helps us all grow as Chimers and individuals.

Chime is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital or family status, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other legally protected basis under provincial, federal, state, and local laws, regulations, or ordinances. We will also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, Cook County Ordinance, NYC Fair Chance Act, and the LA City Fair Chance Ordinance, and consistent with Canadian provincial and federal laws. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation during any stage of the application process, please contact: accommodations@chime.com .

title: Research Engineer, Cybersecurity RL
location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About Horizons

The Horizons team leads Anthropic's reinforcement learning (RL) research and development, playing a critical role in advancing our AI systems. We've contributed to every Claude release, with significant impact on the autonomy, coding, and reasoning capabilities of Anthropic's models.

About the role

We're hiring for the Cybersecurity RL team within Horizons. As a Research Engineer, you'll help to safely advance the capabilities of our models in secure coding, vulnerability remediation, and other areas of defensive cybersecurity.

This role blends research and engineering, requiring you to both develop novel approaches and realize them in code. Your work will include designing and implementing RL environments, conducting experiments and evaluations, delivering your work into production training runs, and collaborating with other researchers, engineers, and cybersecurity specialists across and outside Anthropic.

The role requires domain expertise in cybersecurity paired with interest or experience in training safe AI models. For example, you might be a white hat hacker who's curious about how LLMs could augment or transform your work, a security engineer interested in how AI could help harden systems at scale, or a detection and response professional wondering how models could enhance defensive workflows.

You may be a good fit if you:

•
Have experience in cybersecurity research.

•
Have experience with machine learning.

•
Have strong software engineering skills.

•
Can balance research exploration with engineering implementation.

•
Are passionate about AI's potential and committed to developing safe and beneficial systems.

Strong candidates may also have:

•
Professional experience in security engineering, fuzzing, detection and response, or other applied defensive work.

•
Experience participating in or building CTF competitions and cyber ranges.

•
Academic research experience in cybersecurity.

•
Familiarity with RL techniques and environments.

•
Familiarity with LLM training methodologies.

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:

$500,000 — $850,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. description:
Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.

Software Engineering builds the brains of Waymo's fully autonomous driving technology. Our software allows the Waymo Driver to perceive the world around it, make the right decision for every situation, and deliver people safely to their destinations. We think deeply and solve complex technical challenges in areas like robotics, perception, decision-making and deep learning, while collaborating with hardware and systems engineers. If you’re a software engineer or researcher who’s curious and passionate about Level 4 autonomous driving, we'd like to meet you.

Waymo interns partner with leaders in the industry on projects that create impact to the company. We believe learning is a two-way street: applying your knowledge while providing you with opportunities to expand your skill-set. Interns are an important part of our culture and our recruiting pipeline. Join us at Waymo for a fun and rewarding internship!

You will:

• Design, implement, and scale controllable generation and test-time compute algorithms, multimodal conditioning, and critic-guided flow/diffusion steering—for foundation world models.

• Investigate multimodal sensor + semantic latent conditioning, and representation alignment to advance toward holistic world simulation.

• Leverage learned realism critics and agentic autoresearch workflows on large-scale TPU clusters to evaluate closed-loop interactive realism, long-tail scenario synthesis, and multimodal consistency.

• Write clean, modular, and well-tested JAX code in core simulation and world-modeling codebases, collaborating closely with researchers across Sim Realism, Foundation Models, and Closed-Loop Training teams.

You have:

• Currently pursuing a PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Robotics, or a related technical field, with an anticipated graduation date between December 2027 and August 2028 (returning to a degree program for at least one academic term after the internship).

• Core Implementation Fluency (Mandatory): Strong tensor implementation and debugging skills in Python and JAX/Flax or PyTorch, with hands-on experience training and modifying modern neural architectures (such as Transformers, Diffusion/Flow-Matching models, or deep RL/critic networks).

• Deep Research Expertise in Either: (a) Controllable Generative World / Sequence Modeling & Inference-Time Scaling (hands-on research experience in continuous flow matching / Rectified Flows, score-based diffusion guidance/steering, test-time compute / SMC, or parameter-efficient finetuning) OR (b) Multimodal Spatiotemporal Representation Learning & Closed-Loop Simulation (hands-on research experience in 4D/video tokenization, latent dynamics alignment such as REPA/DINO alignment, inverse RL / adversarial discriminators, or multi-agent trajectory modeling), with working familiarity in the other.

We prefer:

• First-author publications at top-tier machine learning, computer vision, or robotics venues (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR, ECCV, CoRL, RSS, ICRA, or equivalent venues) in generative world models, flow/diffusion steering, controllable generation, or autonomous driving simulation.

Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.

Software Engineering builds the brains of Waymo's fully autonomous driving technology. Our software allows the Waymo Driver to perceive the world around it, make the right decision for every situation, and deliver people safely to their destinations. We think deeply and solve complex technical challenges in areas like robotics, perception, decision-making and deep learning, while collaborating with hardware and systems engineers. If you’re a software engineer or researcher who’s curious and passionate about Level 4 autonomous driving, we'd like to meet you.

Waymo interns partner with leaders in the industry on projects that create impact to the company. We believe learning is a two-way street: applying your knowledge while providing you with opportunities to expand your skill-set. Interns are an important part of our culture and our recruiting pipeline. Join us at Waymo for a fun and rewarding internship!

You will:

  • Design, implement, and scale controllable generation and test-time compute algorithms, multimodal conditioning, and critic-guided flow/diffusion steering—for foundation world models.
  • Investigate multimodal sensor + semantic latent conditioning, and representation alignment to advance toward holistic world simulation.
  • Leverage learned realism critics and agentic autoresearch workflows on large-scale TPU clusters to evaluate closed-loop interactive realism, long-tail scenario synthesis, and multimodal consistency.
  • Write clean, modular, and well-tested JAX code in core simulation and world-modeling codebases, collaborating closely with researchers across Sim Realism, Foundation Models, and Closed-Loop Training teams.

You have:

  • Currently pursuing a PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Robotics, or a related technical field, with an anticipated graduation date between December 2027 and August 2028 (returning to a degree program for at least one academic term after the internship).
  • Core Implementation Fluency (Mandatory): Strong tensor implementation and debugging skills in Python and JAX/Flax or PyTorch, with hands-on experience training and modifying modern neural architectures (such as Transformers, Diffusion/Flow-Matching models, or deep RL/critic networks).
  • Deep Research Expertise in Either: (a) Controllable Generative World / Sequence Modeling & Inference-Time Scaling (hands-on research experience in continuous flow matching / Rectified Flows, score-based diffusion guidance/steering, test-time compute / SMC, or parameter-efficient finetuning) OR (b) Multimodal Spatiotemporal Representation Learning & Closed-Loop Simulation (hands-on research experience in 4D/video tokenization, latent dynamics alignment such as REPA/DINO alignment, inverse RL / adversarial discriminators, or multi-agent trajectory modeling), with working familiarity in the other.

We prefer:

  • First-author publications at top-tier machine learning, computer vision, or robotics venues (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR, ECCV, CoRL, RSS, ICRA, or equivalent venues) in generative world models, flow/diffusion steering, controllable generation, or autonomous driving simulation.
  • Experience with multi-agent closed-loop simulation, counterfactual/adversarial traffic generation, or Sim2Real discriminator/critic stabilization (e.g., Waymax, WOMD, NuPlan, MGAIL, or reward-hacking mitigation).

At Citi, we do not just adapt to change – we drive it. Our Full Time Technology Analyst Program is where forward-thinking talents meet unparalleled opportunities. This is your chance to innovate, influence, and make an impact in the most global financial institution!

Citi Technology partners to ensure that Citi’s platforms can “Be the Best” for clients globally, with a diverse and ethical workforce that applies innovation and automation to deliver a world class client experience and strengthen our reputation. We have over 30,000 technologists globally who are dedicated to serving our clients’ needs across the firm. By utilizing a broad range of technologies, we are at the forefront of innovation. We seek to drive our systems and processes towards scalable, low-latency, high frequency enterprise systems to support Citi’s strategic priorities.

We’re committed to teaching you the ropes. The 2-year Analyst Program starts in July and begins with a robust training program. Here at Citi, rotational programs are intended to help you build a broad skillset and accelerate your career growth by gaining exposure to more than one team. Our rotational program will help you discover the best fit for your skills and long-term career goals at Citi.

Advancing our technological capabilities day after day not only delivers seamless services to the bank but works towards building the flexible systems that will define the digital bank of tomorrow. The Production Support team is at the forefront of maintaining and optimizing critical live production systems, ensuring their health, stability, and peak performance so that Citi can confidently conduct business and service clients. Our analysts use their problem solving and technical skills to quickly resolve any issues, which can vary in severity and complexity and may impact Citi’s reputation or profits. Production support analysts are often ‘the bridge’ between technology and the business, so they quickly become equipped with extensive business knowledge, as well as technical skills.

As a Production Support Analyst, you will work in a dynamic environment that adapts to the needs and priorities of various organizations: Services, Markets, Banking, Functions and Data. This role offers a unique blend of business knowledge and technical expertise, empowering you to swiftly troubleshoot complex problems and engineer robust solutions. Your core mission will be to guarantee production stability, providing an always available and resilient technological backbone for our clients. This involves coordinating with other technology partners such as developers, business teams, etc. to monitor the end-to-end application environment in real-time.

While technologies can vary slightly from team to team, Analysts will have exposure within the following categories :

Gain direct exposure to supporting our clients through the entire lifecycle of incident and problem management. You'll develop critical problem-solving skills and learn how to manage complex technical challenges under pressure.

Contribute to the continuous improvement of our sophisticated monitoring capabilities. You'll work with industry-standard tools like ITRS Geneos and Grafana to build and refine platforms that proactively identify and alert on production issues, enabling rapid resolution.

Unleash your coding potential! You'll have the exciting opportunity to design, develop, and implement custom applications and scripts that automate processes, improve efficiency, and empower your team.

As a Production Support Analyst, you'll master Linux/Unix, hone database expertise (SQL, Oracle, PostgreSQL), and build automation with Python. You'll gain experience with application servers, web technologies, and strengthen networking knowledge. This role offers hands-on use of monitoring tools (ITRS Geneos, Grafana) and exposure to cloud and containerization (Kubernetes), ensuring continuous growth in a dynamic production environment.

While technologies can vary slightly from team to team, Analysts will have exposure within the following categories:

: Java, Spring Framework, Pivotal Cloud Foundry

React or Angular, Apigee TypeScript, HTML5

GitHub Copilot with various models, Citi Squad (automated code reviews), Devin.AI (Agentic Code generation), Prompt Engineering, Workflow Design, GenAI Optimization, Stylus Workspaces (In-house Gemini)

Utilizing tools like Splunk, Tableau, and Adobe Analytics to track customer journey adoption and measure the business value of delivered products.

: Work in globally scoped projects with cross-functional teams and gain insights into how technology drives the financial sector worldwide.

Benefit from structured learning, networking, mentoring, and development programs that are designed to sharpen your technical prowess, enhance your business insight, and cultivate your leadership skills.

: Contribute to real-world projects that shape the future of banking, from developing next-gen digital banking solutions to enhancing our cybersecurity defenses and driving data-powered innovations.

Graduation between Dec 2026 and May 2027.

Educational background: Bachelor’s degree Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Technology, Management Information Systems, or other tech related degrees.

GPA of 3.0 or better is preferred.

A proactive problem-solver who thrives on innovation and embraces challenges with enthusiasm, leveraging Generative AI to address complex business problems and create novel solutions.

Possess a global outlook and willingness to collaborate across cultures and time zones.

Have excellent communication skills, project management, leadership, attention to detail, and the ability to work well within diverse teams.

Ability to pass technical interviews consisting of basic algorithmic programming exercises.

Must be collaborative and adaptable, with excellent communication skills. Prior experience working in agile teams is desirable.

Work Authorization: Authorized to work in United States of America without the need for employer sponsorship, now or in the future.

A steadfast dedication to learning and a true passion for business are vital. As global industries continue to evolve, we are seeking professionals who bring a global perspective to the future of banking and are eager to make an impact at the corporate level using AI. We value diversity and so do you.

Are ambitious, with relentless drive to succeed in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

Are curious about how technology can revolutionize finance and are eager to be at the forefront of this transformation.

Want to grow into a future tech leader, with a passion for both technology and its application in the global financial industry.

Careers that change lives start here. Medtronic is a global leader in healthcare technology with a Mission to alleviate pain, restore health, and extend life. Our 95,000 employees work across more than 150 countries to put patients first — developing innovative medical technologies that improve the lives of 72+ million patients each year. Your unique talents will help shape the future of healthcare while building a career grounded in purpose, growth, and impact.

The Affera Mapping and Ablation System is an innovative medical technology designed to treat patients with cardiac arrhythmias. The system involves advanced mapping techniques to create detailed images of the heart's electrical activity, helping physicians identify abnormal areas causing arrhythmias. Once identified, the Affera Ablation System delivers targeted energy to disrupt these abnormal signals, restoring normal heart rhythm.

This is an onsite position that can sit out of our Mounds View, MN or Newton, MA office.

Medtronic is seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Software Test Engineer to join our Affera Mapping and Ablation System team. This role is essential in supporting the testing and quality assurance processes to ensure the reliability and performance of our advanced medical devices.

This individual will be an integral member in the Affera Software Team, working on cutting-edge technology in the electrophysiology field. This role offers a rare chance to be at the forefront of developing a groundbreaking technology that can disrupt the industry.

The ideal candidate has experience designing, developing and testing real-time high-performance visualization applications. They will take ownership of key features while working collaboratively with other engineering teams, and are passionate about working on a product that will have a positive impact on the lives of millions.

description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the Team

The Security team protects Anthropic's AI systems and maintains the trust of our users and society.

About the Role

At Anthropic, we are pioneering new frontiers in AI that have the potential to greatly benefit society. However, developing advanced AI also comes with risks if not properly safeguarded. As a Research Engineer, you'll help to safely advance the capabilities of our models in incident response, security analysis, vulnerability remediation, and other areas of defensive cybersecurity.

This role blends research and engineering, requiring you to both develop novel approaches and realize them in code. Your work will include designing and implementing RL environments, conducting experiments and evaluations, delivering your work into production training runs, and collaborating with other researchers, engineers, and cybersecurity specialists across and outside Anthropic.

This role requires ML experience combined with domain expertise in cybersecurity. You might be an ML researcher with a history of cybersecurity work, or a security professional with a background in ML.

Responsibilities

• Partner with researchers and safety teams across Anthropic to understand their analytical needs and build solutions

• Develop agentic integrations that allow AI systems to autonomously investigate and act on analytical findings

• Contribute to the strategic direction of the team, including decisions about what to build, what to partner on, and where to invest

• This role may require participation in an on-call rotation.

You may be a good fit if you

• Have experience with machine learning.

• Have experience in cybersecurity research.

• Have strong software engineering skills.

• Can balance research exploration with engineering implementation.

• Are passionate about AI's potential and committed to developing safe and beneficial systems.

Strong candidates may also have

• Professional experience in security engineering, fuzzing, detection and response, or other applied defensive work.

• Experience participating in or building CTF competitions and cyber ranges.

• Academic research experience in cybersecurity or other experimental & research background.

• Familiarity with RL techniques and environments.

• Familiarity with LLM training methodologies.

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:

$1 — $2 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

description:
We're Scan.com . We're building America's national imaging network: the infrastructure that connects patients, providers, and payers to faster, better-value diagnostic imaging. Thousands of patients move through our platform every day, and each is a real person waiting for an answer to a healthcare concern. We exist to get them that answer faster.

We manage the medical imaging pathway end-to-end. Providers order through a single point of entry, and from there, we run the entire medical diagnostic pathway. Managing the full pathway, rather than brokering pieces of it, is what lets us deliver imaging faster, at higher quality, and at a lower cost than the fragmented status quo.

We're looking for a

at an exciting time. We've raised over $200m in funding to date, reached profitability, and are growing 100% year on year.

Millions of people wait too long for a diagnosis. Come help us fix that.

Scan.com 's integration layer is mission-critical infrastructure. We interface with hundreds of imaging centers and health systems operating disparate, often decades-old systems — RIS platforms built on legacy protocols, HL7 v2 feeds with idiosyncratic vendor dialects, and hardware gateways running in constrained clinical environments. On the demand side, we connect to modern EHR APIs, third-party referral networks, and portal integrations that must work reliably at scale.

, you will architect and build the systems that make the demand-side connections robust, observable, and extensible. This problem area requires genuine passion for system integration patterns, message transformation pipelines, and the operational discipline to maintain high-reliability infrastructure in the face of real-world entropy.

As a scale-up business, you can expect your role to develop over time. Here are some of the types of things you could be getting involved in:

Build and maintain integration connectors for modern and legacy EHR systems to retrieve physician referrals and relevant patient documentation.

Architect a fault-tolerant message queuing and delivery infrastructure for inbound and outbound HL7 and API traffic.

Build and maintain REST API integrations with third-party referral sources, attorney platforms, and demand aggregators.

Own the observability layer for the integration infrastructure: structured logging, alerting on message processing latency/failures, and dashboards that surface issues before they reach the operations teams.

Within 90 days, you have a complete mental model of our integration workflows — every active connector, its transport mechanism, its failure modes, and its monitoring coverage.

You have identified and remediated the most critical reliability gaps in our referral pipeline. There is a measurable reduction in integration-related operational escalations.

You have designed or materially evolved our data workflows such that onboarding a new demand-side source is a simple choice from a menu of robust technical options.

Every integration has structured alerting and a clear SLA. The operations team can self-serve integration health for routine issues without engineering involvement.

At least two significant referral integration improvements. This can be new connectors that significantly increase referral volume, automations that improve quality, or infrastructure improvements. These improvements are live in production and have measurably increased referral volume, improved connection optionality, operational efficiency, and reduced error rates.

You don't need to tick all the boxes to apply for this role. Whether it's your first role or your fifth, we believe everyone can add value, learn, and grow. However, these might be some of the ways you are currently adding value:

Proven ability to integrate with legacy systems that were not designed for modern interoperability. For example, aging RIS platforms in radiology, core banking systems in fintech, or equivalent legacy infrastructure in another vertical. The underlying pattern of bridging old and new matters more than the specific domain.

Proficiency in at least one backend language used in high-reliability integration contexts (Python, Ruby, Java, C# are all relevant; language is less important than architectural rigor).

Familiarity with RESTful API integration patterns, including schema versioning, backward compatibility, and API contract management

Strong operational instincts: you instrument what you build, you think about failure modes before they happen, and you treat on-call escalations as a signal about systemic gaps

Bias for innovation: You care about questioning the ‘why’ behind every system, and have a strong desire to build the next generation of products you work on.

Experience in healthcare is a plus, but not required. We care far more about your engineering depth and API design fluency than your industry background

If we're not growing, we're dying. Everyone needs a bias for action. Speed and momentum, combined with quality execution, propel our business forward.

You don't quit on hard problems. Fail fast, dust off, go again.

You celebrate wins, then seek the next opportunity.

You see it, you fix it. No task is beneath you, at any level.

The company we build is the team we build. If we don't have the right people in the right seats, doing the right things, we will fail.

Talent recognizes talent. You actively bring quality hires into the business.

You trust your colleagues to deliver.

You open-source your knowledge. You're never a single point of failure.

Care enough to have the hard conversations, and don't dwell on them. Don't go up the chain to communicate. Go straight to the person.

Strong opinions, weakly held. You welcome challenge and feedback.

You get to the point: direct challenge plus an alternative solution.

You ask "why". Before calling something bad, understand why it exists.

Push the limits of your understanding and potential and you will be supported to get better.

You proactively seek feedback, whatever your level.

You invest in understanding our business: teams, customers, processes.

You invest in your own growth and are willing to unlearn.

We're a high-performing team with low ego. We hire people who are brilliant and kind, who give it straight, back it up with evidence, and change their mind when the facts change. We'll give you real ownership early, the tools to do the best work of your career, and colleagues who raise your game. In return, we ask for high standards, genuine care for patients and each other, and the drive to leave things better than you found them. If that sounds like you, let’s talk!

We keep our interview process short and sweet, and we're a nimble team that can progress at pace. Here are the stages you can expect, but we might switch up the order of each step depending on team availability:

title: Forward Deployed Solutions Engineer
location: Denver, CO - Hybrid; New York, NY - Hybrid; San Francisco, CA - Hybrid; Scottsdale, AZ - Hybrid
description:
About Gusto

At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.

All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy .

AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.

About the Role

This is a highly customer-facing role at the intersection of engineering, solution architecture, agentic AI, and customer delivery. You will work directly with stakeholders and own the technical discovery for our ongoing opportunities end to end. Once a deal is qualified, you scope, build, embed with the client, and build it yourself, code that holds up against real tax and jurisdiction data, not a prototype you clean up later. What you ship only counts once the client is paying for it, it's live, and it's measurably cutting the manual work they used to do by hand, hours saved, tickets deflected, risk reduced. You should be comfortable speaking with both technical and executive stakeholders, moving quickly from problem discovery to prototype, and turning complex workflows into production-ready agents and multi-agent systems.

Here's what you'll do day-to-day

• Scope & Qualify: Give Sales a technical feasibility read early on ambiguous Enterprise opportunities, then own scoping the compliance challenge once the deal is sales-qualified.

• Define the Problem: Own requirements gathering on complex, ambiguous opportunities, scoping the problem clearly enough for Sales, Product, and Engineering to align on it.

• Prove It First: Build a working proof-of-concept of the proposed agent when a deal needs to see feasibility before committing to the full build, tailored from a hands-on integration engineer to a VP of Payroll Tax.

• Make the Business Case: Translate every deployment into the business case that justifies the subscription: hours saved, risk reduced, compliance simplified.

• Own the Build: Embed with clients and write the code yourself, work that runs their compliance decisions instead of just connecting to them. There's no fixed method yet, you figure out what each engagement needs and build it.

• Clear the Blockers: Diagnose and fix the data issues, jurisdiction mapping, tax ID reconciliation, that stand between a client and production.

• Bridge the Gap: Keep technical teams and business stakeholders aligned as requirements evolve mid-engagement, so scope changes don't blindside either side.

• Own the Handoff: Deliver the build and a runbook Client Success runs solo without the need to loop back the FDE.

• Close the Loop: Feed structured signal from both the sales motion and the build motion back into product and go-to-market strategy, including infrastructure gaps.

• Create Implementation Playbooks: solution patterns, demo flows, and deployment documentation that make future deployments faster.

Here's what we're looking for

• Demonstrated 5+ years of hands-on experience in a customer-facing technical role such as Forward Deployed Engineer, Solutions Engineer, AI Engineer, Implementation Engineer, Solutions Architect, Technical Consultant, or similar.

• Proven track record of shipping production systems in ambiguous, client-facing environments, with demonstrable evidence of:

• REST APIs, webhooks, event-driven systems, auth patterns, data modeling, idempotency, and failure modes, not just happy-path builds

• Building production systems in highly regulated categories, payroll, tax, or compliance fluency deep enough to run a conversation with a client's compliance team without a translator

• Agentic workflows beyond prototypes: MCP or function-calling patterns, evaluation and reliability practices

• Deep technical discovery skills with the ability to navigate a high degree of ambiguity

• Ability to scope a technical solution from an ambiguous opportunity, build the business case that justifies a subscription, and ship a pattern the next engagement can reuse

• Proven ability to present to and influence a range of audiences, from individual engineers to executive sponsors

• Entrepreneurial, passionate about our mission, and deep empathy for the clients whose compliance work you're automating

• Bonus points for experience with a specific HR/payroll platform's integration surface, enterprise procurement or security review processes, or MEDDPICC-style deal frameworks

Who Thrives Here

Builders who can sit with a customer, understand the real problem, quickly build an agentic solution, and present it clearly enough that the customer immediately sees the value.

You’ll thrive here if you are technical, customer-facing, fast-moving, and independent. You prototype and debug rather than only coordinate. You take responsibility for the customer outcome, communicate proactively, flag risks early, and follow through. You are comfortable being the technical adult in the room, whether you’re speaking with a customer’s architect, operations lead, engineering team, or VP of Payroll.

We’re looking for someone low-ego, collaborative, sharp, and highly accountable - someone who can build trust with customers while also building real technical solutions.

Our total cash compensation amount for this role is targeted at $88,000-140,000 in Scottsdale, $95,000-150,000 in Denver, and $115,000-181,000 in New York & San Francisco Bay Area. Stock equity is additional. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors including candidate experience and expertise and may vary from the amounts listed above.

At Gusto, we don't use titles the traditional way, as a signal of rank or hierarchy. Instead, our titles describe two things at once — your craft (what you do, e.g. Engineering, Design) and your scope of ownership (what you're accountable for) — which is why you'll see something like "Head of X" instead of a rank word like "Director" that tells you neither. Because of this, the title on this posting may look different from what you'd expect based on the scope and seniority of the role, and from how similar roles are typically titled elsewhere. If you have questions about how this role compares to your current title or level, your recruiter can help translate.

Gusto has physical office spaces in Denver, San Francisco, and New York City. Employees who are based in those locations will be expected to work from the office on designated days approximately 2-3 days per week (or more depending on role). The same office expectations apply to all Symmetry roles, Gusto's subsidiary, whose physical office is in Scottsdale.

Note: The San Francisco office expectations encompass both the San Francisco and San Jose metro areas.

When approved to work from a location other than a Gusto office, a secure, reliable, and consistent internet connection is required. This includes non-office days for hybrid employees.

Reliable, consistent presence: We expect regular and predictable attendance, whether you're working in-office, hybrid, or fully remote, so that you stay closely connected to your team, customers, and stakeholders in real time and ensure colleagues and customers receive the timely support and responsiveness they deserve.

Our customers come from all walks of life and so do we. We hire great people from a wide variety of backgrounds, not just because it's the right thing to do, but because it makes our company stronger. If you share our values and our enthusiasm for small businesses, you will find a home at Gusto.

Gusto is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate in hiring or any employment decision based on race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, genetic information, veteran status, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. Gusto considers qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law. Gusto is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application procedures. We want to see our candidates perform to the best of their ability. If you require a medical or religious accommodation at any time throughout your candidate journey, please fill out this form and a member of our team will get in touch with you.

Gusto takes security and protection of your personal information very seriously. Please review our Fraudulent Activity Disclaimer .

Personal information collected and processed as part of your Gusto application will be subject to Gusto's Applicant Privacy Notice .

title: PhD Intern, Software Engineer - Interaction Design (2027)
location: San Francisco, CA • New York, NY
description:
Figma is growing our team of passionate creatives and builders on a mission to make design accessible to all. Figma’s platform helps teams bring ideas to life—whether you're brainstorming, creating a prototype, translating designs into code, or iterating with AI. From idea to product, Figma empowers teams to streamline workflows, move faster, and work together in real time from anywhere in the world. If you're excited to shape the future of design and collaboration, join us!

Figma’s Interaction Design team helps designers express how interactive experiences behave from a single interaction, to a multi-state flow, to a series of complex animated transitions. We’re interested in making complex interactive behavior easier to author, refine and understand. This team investigates and identifies new ways to visualize and manage state, animations, interactions, and prototypes through click-through and code-backed experiences.

As a PhD intern, you’ll combine HCI research with hands-on-engineering to help define the next generation of interactive experience design tooling. You’ll work closely with a mentor and teammates and get to learn, contribute, and grow in a supportive environment, while applying your research background to drive real-world impact.

This 12 or 16-week internship for Summer 2027 will be based out of our San Francisco or New York hub.

What you’ll do at Figma:

• Be fully embedded onto a Figma team working on problems that intersect with your research area

• Drive projects that apply research insights to meaningful product challenges

• Collaborate with engineers, PMs, designers, and researchers to scope and execute your work

To get the best candidate experience, please consider applying for a maximum of 3 roles within 12 months to ensure you are not duplicating efforts.

Our Futureforce University Recruiting program is dedicated to attracting, retaining and cultivating talent. Our interns and new graduates work on real projects that affect how our business runs, giving them

to make a tangible impact on the future of our company. With offices all over the world, our recruits have the chance to collaborate and connect with fellow employees on a global scale. We offer job shadowing, mentorship programs, talent development courses, and much more.

Enterprise Technology & Infrastructure

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

TITLE: Service Management - Analyst, Global Sector

The Experience

Salesforce Global Sector is now our fastest growing industry business at scale, growing 80% year over year. We help organizations modernize their operations, strengthen trust, and deliver mission-critical outcomes with the power of the #1 AI CRM.

Behind that growth is an equally important opportunity to transform how our own Sector teams operate. We build secure, scalable, and compliant solutions that enable Salesforce teams across Sales, Professional Services, and Customer Success to serve highly regulated customers with greater speed, confidence, and efficiency, while creating a trusted digital foundation for continued growth.

We are seeking a Service Management Analyst to help build the next generation of AI-powered engineering. Join our AI-native team as an early-career service manager to solve real production challenges, build intelligent automation and strengthen system reliability. With hands-on guidance from a senior mentor, you'll combine AI-assisted investigational skills with production support experience to grow into broader product or technical roles.

You'll investigate support cases, troubleshoot production issues and participate in support rotations—gaining firsthand insight into how complex systems work and where they can improve. Your mandate goes beyond resolving individual issues: you'll adopt and nurture AI-assisted solutions that eliminate recurring manual work and prevent problems from returning.

Your projects could include agentic case automation, trend analysis, automated access workflows, technical knowledge retrieval, log analysis and system hardening. You'll have the opportunities to own improvements from identifying the problem to measuring the result. It's a chance to learn through practical ownership, deliver meaningful improvements and build a foundation for a successful support & services career.

Must be a U.S. Citizen operating on U.S. Soil with ability to meet customer and government screening standards applicable to this role, including a Criminal Justice Information Services screening with fingerprint scan. Due to the citizenship requirement for this role, which supports U.S. federal, state, and/or local government customers, citizenship will be verified through two of the following REAL ID Act documents: U.S. Passport, Passport Card, REAL Driver's License, Global Entry Card, U.S. Government CAC/PIV.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

Production Support & Monitoring Monitor daily batch jobs, system health dashboards, and application alerts to catch and address anomalies before they impact end-users.

Incident & Problem Management Participate in incident response and scheduled support or on-call rotations, with training and guidance appropriate to your experience.

Triage, troubleshoot, and document incoming production incidents (P1/P2 events), coordinate fix actions, and assist with root-cause analysis (RCA).

Partner with Engineering to improve code, monitoring, tests and documentation to prevent recurring incidents.

Application Lifecycle & Service Management Track application performance metrics, maintenance windows, and compliance checks aligned with ITIL Service Operation frameworks.

Support to Salesforce Security mandates and best practices such as certification & token refresh, password rotation, QAR and federal audits.

Ticket & Request Handling Manage service request fulfillment, user access coordination, and vendor-escalated support tickets within established SLAs.

Support Production Deployments

Tools & Automations Build automation for recurring tasks such as access requests, case responses, log analysis, troubleshooting and maintenance.

Develop AI agents and workflows that help classify cases, retrieve relevant knowledge and execute approved actions with appropriate safeguards.

Help train AI agents to stay up-to-date, improve accuracy and efficiency.

Cross-Functional Collaboration Act as an operational touchpoint between site IT, software engineering teams, and external third-party software vendors.

Reporting & Documentation Compile operational KPI reports, update runbooks and knowledge-base articles, and document recurring system anomalies or process gaps.

You're Our Person If...

A technical background, such as an MIS degree or a CS minor, with an understanding of computer systems and troubleshooting. Writing code is not required.

A Salesforce Platform Administrator I certification. The advanced certification can come after joining.

At least one internship or some industry experience

Willingness to work swing shifts and take PagerDuty on-call rotation

An ability to investigate problems using logs, error messages and system behavior.

Clear communication, a collaborative approach and a willingness to ask questions and learn from feedback.

Self-starter, willing to learn new technologies (Mulesoft, AI, Agentforce) and a Salesforce trailblazer who thrives on working in a fast-paced environment.

Ability to engage with self awareness as required to avoid conflicts with customers based on personality differences and to make suggestions in a manner that is more likely to result in a desired outcome.

Even Better If...

Experience with sandboxes and deployments, and familiarity with Salesforce enterprise environment, SOX protocols, Change Management and Release Management standards

Platform or Salesforce internship experience, familiarity with PagerDuty or incident management, and basic AI literacy

Curiosity and a passion for helping end users discover and resolve issues, asking good questions, breaking problems down and thinking on your feet

Initiative, such as self-study or certifying on your own, and comfort with operational, on-call work

The Service Management Analyst serves as an individual contributor within the operations and service management team. This role monitors core applications, resolves or escalates production incidents, tracks Service Level Agreements (SLAs), and supports continuous operational improvement. You will work closely with engineering, vendor partners, and business stakeholders to ensure application stability, data integrity, smooth incident workflows and standards.

We welcome evidence of your skills from internships, coursework, personal projects, open-source contributions or professional experience. The scope and independence expected will reflect the level of the role.

Unleash Your Potential

When you join Salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. Our benefits and resources support you to find balance and be your best , and our AI agents accelerate your impact so you can do your best . Together, we’ll bring the power of Agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love. Apply today to not only shape the future — but to redefine what’s possible — for yourself, for AI, and the world.

Accommodations

If you need a reasonable accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please submit a request via this Accommodations Request Form .

Please note that Salesforce uses artificial intelligence (AI) tools to help our recruiters assess and evaluate candidates’ resumes and qualifications throughout the recruiting process. Humans will always make any candidate selection and hiring decisions. Please see our Candidate Privacy Statement for more information about how we use your personal data and your rights, including with regard to use of AI tools and opt out options.

description:
We are seeking a Junior Quality Assurance Engineer to join our QA team and grow into automation. The role begins with functional and regression testing, test data preparation and defect reporting, and builds toward authoring automated tests with support from a senior engineer.

The ideal candidate is methodical, curious about how the system works underneath the screen, and wants to build an engineering career in quality rather than only execute scripts.
title: QA Engineer
qualifications: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
+ years of software testing experience, including internship or placement experience.
Exposure to automated testing, whether professional, academic or self-taught.
Working SQL, enough to query and validate data independently.
Familiarity with at least one automation framework such as Playwright, Selenium or Cypress.
Some programming exposure in TypeScript, JavaScript, C# or Python.
Familiarity with source control or a work tracking tool such as Azure DevOps, Jira or Aha.
Understanding of Agile and Scrum delivery.
Attention to detail and the discipline to record results accurately.
Willingness to say when something is unclear rather than guess the expected result.
Clear written communication in defect reports and status updates.
Exposure to API testing with Postman or similar.
Exposure to accessibility testing or tools such as axe-core, Lighthouse or NVDA.
Exposure to AI-assisted testing tools.
responsibilities: Execute functional, integration and regression test cases against assigned products and record results with evidence.
Write test cases from requirements and acceptance criteria. Tests must never be written from the application under test, because code-derived tests treat existing defects as correct behavior.
Maintain the regression suite for an assigned product and flag coverage gaps.
Support release testing and production verification.
Create and maintain test data, including records that trigger validation and error paths.
Validate results in the database using SQL where the user interface does not show the full picture.
Reconcile data between systems on conversion and integration work.
Run existing automated suites, triage failures and report whether the cause is the product or the test.
Author and extend automated tests in the existing framework with support from a senior engineer.
Grow toward owning automation for an assigned module.
Use approved AI tools and team prompts to draft test cases and automation.
Review every AI-generated artefact against the requirement before it is used. The requirement decides what is correct, not the generated output.

Schneider Electric is seeking a Technical Support Engineer in Fort Collins, CO to support their GIS software solution. Schneider Electric delivers Information Technology for a sustainable and secure world.

Schneider Electric delivers sustainable smart electric grid solutions – offering proven, real-time information management tools and practical utility experience. Its complete Smart Grid Solution suite is built on a single data model available across the enterprise for optimized decision making.

This integrated, scalable solution will let utilities efficiently plan, design, operate and evolve a reliable and efficient smart electric grid for the benefit of customers and the environment, today and tomorrow. At the source of Schneider Electric’s success are its people.

Technical Support Engineers at Schneider Electric are highly capable technical professionals. We are looking for individuals who like to research, use tools to dig deep into complex issues, and enjoy looking at code to aid in their troubleshooting. Support Engineers work independently and as members of a small team to resolve technical software issues for clients. Support team members serve as one of the main contacts to a client base that is knowledgeable, technical, and often in operation-critical functions at utility companies. Support Engineers play a significant role in creating and maintaining the client relationship that is valuable to our organization. Technical issues we address range across database configuration, software defects, and user education.

description:
From the beginning, Starbucks set out to be a different kind of company. One that not only celebrated coffee and the rich tradition, but that also brought a feeling of connection. We are known for developing extraordinary leaders who share this passion and are guided by their service to others.

As the engineer I, you will play a critical role in advancing our enterprise technology solutions, supporting the platforms that underpin in-store partner tooling. This role sits at the intersection of Partner Tech, Retail Operations, and Enterprise Data & Analytics, driving platform-based solutions that balance standardization, flexibility, and innovation at scale.

You will execute the strategy, engineering, and delivery for Digital Experience platforms, ensuring these systems operate as enterprise-grade, resilient, and extensible capabilities that unlock business outcomes—not just point solutions. These products are at the heart of shift execution and should increasingly leverage AI and intelligent automation to improve productivity, accelerate decision-making, and enhance problem solving for partners and operators

As an engineer I, you will...

Build, iterate, and enhance iOS applications used by Starbucks partners to support store readiness and day-to-day store experiences.

Deliver accessible, reliable, maintainable, and well-tested features from implementation through production.

Contribute to technical design, architecture discussions, code reviews, and the evolution of mobile engineering practices.

Integrate iOS applications with GraphQL APIs, REST APIs, and backend services.

Collaborate across product, design, backend, QA, and engineering teams to deliver end-to-end solutions.

Improve application quality through unit, integration, and automated UI testing.

Diagnose and resolve application defects, crashes, performance issues, and reliability problems.

Participate in CI/CD, application releases, production support, and incident-resolution activities.

Contribute to technical documentation, operational runbooks, team tooling, and knowledge sharing.

Use AI-assisted development tools thoughtfully across development, testing, debugging, documentation, and code review.

Apply appropriate judgment when reviewing AI-generated solutions to maintain standards for quality, security, testing, and maintainability.

Continue developing broader technical ownership across mobile development, backend integration, and application delivery.

-2+ years of professional software-development experience, including professional iOS development experience.

Strong proficiency with Swift and experience developing applications using SwiftUI and/or UIKit.

Experience with Swift concurrency, asynchronous programming, networking, application lifecycle, and state management.

Experience integrating iOS applications with GraphQL APIs, including data modeling, queries, mutations, error handling, caching, and resilient client-server interactions.

Experience integrating mobile applications with REST APIs and backend services.

Understanding of modern iOS architecture, modular application development, state management, and dependency management.

Experience writing unit and integration tests and familiarity with automated UI testing.

Experience with Git, pull requests, code reviews, branching, and collaborative software-development workflows.

Familiarity with CI/CD and automated mobile build, test, and deployment pipelines.

Experience debugging application defects, crashes, and performance issues using Xcode, logging, profiling, and application-monitoring tools.

Familiarity with application health and observability, including crash analysis, performance monitoring, and production diagnostics.

Understanding of secure mobile development, authentication, authorization, secure token handling, and application-data protection.

Experience delivering features through the software-development lifecycle, including implementation, testing, deployment, monitoring, and production support.

Ability to work effectively in an Agile product team and collaborate across product, design, backend engineering, QA, and operations.

Experience using AI-assisted development tools or agents, with an understanding of the importance of reviewing and validating AI-generated code and recommendations.

As a Starbucks partner, you (and your family) will have access to medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, and other voluntary insurance benefits. Partners have access to short-term and long-term disability, paid parental leave, family expansion reimbursement, paid vacation from date of hire*, sick time (accrued at 1 hour for every 25 hours worked), eight paid holidays, and two personal days per year. Starbucks also offers eligible partners participation in a 401(k) retirement plan with employer match, a discounted company stock program (S.I.P.), Starbucks equity program (Bean Stock), incentivized emergency savings, and financial well-being tools. Additionally, Starbucks offers 100% upfront tuition coverage for a first-time bachelor’s degree through Arizona State University’s online program via the Starbucks College Achievement Plan, student loan management resources, and access to other educational opportunities. You will also have access to backup care and DACA reimbursement. Starbucks will comply with any applicable state and local laws regarding employee leave benefits, including, but not limited to providing time off pursuant to the Colorado Healthy Families and Workplaces Act, and in accordance with its plans and policies. This list is subject to change depending on collective bargaining in locations where partners have a certified bargaining representative. For additional information regarding partner perks and more detailed information about benefits, go to starbucksbenefits.com.

If you are working in CA, CO, IL, LA, ME, MA, NE, ND or RI, you will accrue vacation up to a maximum of 120 hours (190 in CA) for roles below director and 200 hours (316 in CA) for roles at director or above. For roles in other states, you will be granted vacation time starting at 120 hours annually for roles below director and 200 hours annually for roles director and above.

The actual base pay offered to the successful candidate will be based on multiple factors, including but not limited to job-related knowledge/skills, experience, geographical location, and internal equity. At Starbucks, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at the high end of the range for their role, and compensation decisions are dependent upon the facts and circumstances of each position and candidate.

description:
The Enterprise Technology Services organization partners with every part of the American Express business to power the company’s growth and innovation with trust and efficiency, and drive competitive differentiation with speed. We support the delivery and operations of technology, digital, and data capabilities, platforms, and services globally. Specifically, our team is responsible for the company’s technology engineering, architecture, and infrastructure, providing 24x7 support to ensure an uninterrupted, high-quality experience for customers and colleagues. We also provide product management for core enterprise platforms, and lead technology risk and information security, enterprise data governance and platforms, digital product and design, and enterprise AI platforms on behalf of the company.

At American Express, we empower future technologists to learn, innovate, and make an impact from day one. As a Software Engineer Intern, you’ll join a 10-week Summer Internship Program and contribute to real-world technology projects that support seamless customer and colleague experiences. You’ll build software, collaborate with Agile teams, and learn how products are designed, developed, tested, and delivered in a global enterprise environment. These skills will give you the tools to accelerate in your studies and future career!

Enterprise Technology Services teams build and operate technology that helps American Express deliver trusted, secure, and customer first products and services. Interns may be aligned to scrum teams across backend engineering, frontend engineering, cloud engineering, mobile, AI/machine learning, data oriented engineering, or full-stack product development. The role family is Software Engineering which means designing, coding, testing, and improving applications and services that help customers, colleagues, and partners get work done reliably and securely.

About Americanexpress:
At American Express, our culture is built on a 175-year history of innovation, shared values and Leadership Behaviors, and an unwavering commitment to back our customers, communities, and colleagues. From delivering differentiated products to providing world-class customer service, we operate with a strong risk mindset, ensuring we continue to uphold our brand promise of trust, security, and servi

Bachelor’s degree candidates with an expected graduation date between December 2027 and June 2028.

Demonstrated experience through coursework, projects, research, or extracurricular activities using one or more programming languages such as Java, JavaScript, Python, C#, Go, Kotlin, or similar technologies.
Foundational understanding of computer science concepts including data structures, algorithms, object-oriented programming, debugging, and problem solving.
Interest in building software applications across web, mobile, backend, cloud, API, or full-stack environments.
Familiarity with modern software development practices such as version control, testing, code reviews, Agile methodologies, and collaborative development workflows.
Curiosity and enthusiasm for emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, intelligent automation, and AI-powered developer tools.
Strong communication, teamwork, and collaboration skills with the ability to learn quickly, seek feedback, and work effectively in a diverse and inclusive environment.
Preferred Qualifications
A curious, collaborative problem solver who enjoys learning new technologies and applying them to practical challenges.
Understanding and experience leveraging AI powered development tools, generative AI, intelligent automation, responsible AI, and machine learning fundamentals.

A student who has built and programmed software through academic, personal, internship, open-source, hackathon, or project-based experiences.
Someone who communicates clearly, welcomes feedback, and brings an inclusive, customer first mindset to team environments.
Technology Areas for Software Engineers

American Express Software Engineering Interns may be aligned to different technology teams based on business needs, project requirements, and individual strengths. Experience in one or more of the following areas is beneficial:
Back-End Engineering: Java, Python, Golang, APIs, microservices, Big Data, or Data Engineering concepts.
Front-End Engineering: JavaScript, React, TypeScript, REST APIs, accessibility, and user experience principles.
Cloud Engineering: Java, Python, cloud-native development, microservices, CI/CD, containerization, and DevOps practices.
Site Reliability Engineer: Knowledge of observability tools and methodologies, including experience with logging, monitoring, tracing, and performance analysis platforms
AI & Machine Learning Engineering: Java, Python, machine learning fundamentals, AI powered development tools, agentic workflows, AI agents, data processing, automation, and responsible AI concepts.

Core Skills Across All Areas: Strong problem-solving abilities, computer science fundamentals, communication and collaboration skills, experience working in team environments, and curiosity for emerging technologies including Artificial Intelligence and Generative AI.
Our team reviews applications on a rolling basis. We appreciate your patience while we consider your application and will contact qualified candidates regarding next steps.
Employment eligibility to work with American Express in the United States is required as the company will not pursue visa sponsorship for these positions.
